- Penicillin allergy: hives
- Seasonal allergies in May: managed with Reactine

Glad that works. For the mithai I'd go with Brijwasi Sweets: best freshness reviews, Rs 1,450 plus Rs 120 delivery, and same day if ordered before 14:00 IST. I just need your mom's delivery address. Action: Hold the order until you send the address, then place it.

'To Neha and [partner's name]: you two make the rest of us look bad at being a couple, and we have never been happier about it. Neha, you finally found someone who puts up with you before coffee, which honestly is the real engagement here. To the happy couple, may your arguments always be about where to eat, never what to eat. Cheers!'

Action: I need her partner's name to fill the blank; send it to me and I'll tidy the toast, or tell me a funny story about Neha to work in.

Congratulations on the half marathon, 2:04:37 on the waterfront is a huge result, and it's great that Marcus got you through it. I'll set a Friday 15:00 reminder to post the payouts status update in #payouts-launch by 16:00, with a pre-draft from Linear (five bullets, red/amber/green per workstream), and keep Friday evenings clear for pizza and movie night. That's rough, a coat at your desk is a sign the thermostat won. Action: None; if you want, ask facilities to turn the floor's AC down and I'll draft the message.

I don't have the Dec 13 answer in front of me, and I don't want to guess the quantities for the bag recipe. Try: 'When a payout fails because of a bank-side error, the system shall automatically retry the payout without requiring merchant intervention.' It drops the stacked clauses but keeps the requirement intact. Action: Paste it into the PRD in place of the old sentence when you're happy with it.

Sent your thank-you text to Hannah. For Grace, a sparkling mocktail: muddled lime and mint with ginger beer and a splash of cranberry, served in a proper glass with a rosemary sprig. The earlier fares I'd found (WestJet $642, Air Canada $689 return) were for the August long weekend, so they aren't a like-for-like comparison and I'd need to pull up that search to confirm. I don't have the Lafourcade song thing and don't want to guess. Action: Re-run the flight comparison for the July dates and send Kabir the numbers, and ask you what the Lafourcade song thing was so I can send it to Mei.

Aisha prefers async, so I'll also link her edge-case doc and drop a note in her Slack thread. I don't have your reason for the cuts, so I'll leave a placeholder for it. Action: Draft the Slack message to Aisha for your approval and set a Thursday reminder to check her reply.

Here's what Jess should weigh:
- Cash flow: will rent cover the mortgage, condo fees, property tax and insurance, with a buffer for vacancies?
- Taxes: rental income is taxable, and renting out the unit can affect the principal-residence exemption.
- Market view: selling locks in today's price; holding is a bet on appreciation.
- Landlord effort: tenants, repairs, and what happens if things go wrong.
- Her plans: if she might move back, renting keeps that option open.
An hour with an accountant or fee-only planner would settle the tax part. Action: None.

I can check, but I need the old pricing page URL to search for (and the new one to swap in). Action: Once you send the old URL, search your docs and the beta materials for it, list every file that still links to it with the new link suggested, and not change anything until you approve.

Action: Keep it as a draft until you say send, then text it to Hannah.

Here's the plan for your drill sheet, built around role-play with Mexican vocabulary (carro, computadora). Three sections: ser vs estar with emotions and locations, por vs para, and the subjunctive after 'cuando' for future events, with your example corrected to 'cuando llegue a casa te llamo'. Each gets fill-in-the-blank items plus a short role-play scenario, like a work meeting, to practise them. Action: Build the sheet with an answer key, save it to your notes, and have it ready before your next lesson with Carlos.

Roughly, a heat warning is issued when hot days and warm nights are expected for about two days, and an extended heat warning means that heat is expected to last longer, around three or more days, so cooling-centre type measures usually kick in. I'd double-check exact thresholds on Environment Canada since they differ by region. Action: Check which alert is in effect for Toronto and tell you if the phone buzzing is the extended one.

A common rule of thumb: a retention curve has flattened when the drop between consecutive periods is only about a point or two, or the slope is near zero, for three or more periods in a row. Ideally that holds across several cohorts, and the plateau should sit well above zero. Newer cohorts flattening at a lower level than older ones is a warning sign. Action: If you share the curve, I'll check it against that rule.

I'd go with ChessKid: it's built for kids, moderated, and has no ads, though the full version needs a paid subscription. A free alternative is Lichess, which is ad-free but not made for kids. Action: Check the current ChessKid pricing and in-app purchase settings before you install, and see which app the school club uses.

I'll update Biscuit's vet to Dr. Kaur at Riverside Veterinary Clinic on Broadview Ave, replacing Dr. Moreau. For next week I'll look for a weekday slot after 5:30 pm for his annual shots and rabies booster. Action: Update the contact, check Riverside's availability and your calendar for next week, and book the best slot, then confirm it with you.

Cardboard fort supplies, beyond the boxes in the basement:
- Packing or duct tape (strong), and a box cutter or scissors for you to cut
- Markers or paint for doors and windows
- Blankets or sheets and clothespins for a roof
- A flashlight or string lights, and pillows for inside
Action: Make a checklist note and check what you already have so you only buy what's missing, probably tape.

EFT is the broad term for any electronic transfer of funds between accounts. ACH is the US system's name (Automated Clearing House); in Canada the equivalent bank-to-bank rails are run through Payments Canada, so people often say EFT for direct deposits and pre-authorized debits. People on your call were probably using ACH loosely to mean EFT. Action: None.

I'll leave Netflix, Spotify Family, Crave and the Globe and Mail as they are. RRSP: you get a tax deduction now and pay tax when you withdraw, so it favours higher income today than in retirement. TFSA: no deduction, but growth and withdrawals are tax-free and the room comes back, so it's more flexible. Action: None.
